title: Boss: the container help desk
summary: Tickets from teammates whose containers misbehave. Turn your mental model into tools that diagnose them.

steps.title: Your queue
steps.body: You are the person the team asks when "Docker is broken". Most tickets come down to three things: the app is not reachable, the container stopped, or two names are secretly the same image. Build a small tool for each.

steps.title: Why can't I reach it?
prompt: Write `string Reach(string publish, string listenAddress, int listenPort)`.
- `publish` is the `-p` value used (`"8080:80"`, `"127.0.0.1:8080:80"`) or `""` when nothing was published.
- `listenAddress` and `listenPort` describe where the app listens **inside** the container.
Check in this order and return the first that applies:
2. `listenAddress` is `127.0.0.1` → `unreachable: app listens on 127.0.0.1 inside the container; bind to 0.0.0.0`
3. container port in the spec differs from `listenPort` → `unreachable: app listens on 3000 but 80 is published` (with the real numbers)
4. otherwise → `http://localhost:8080` (or `http://IP:PORT` when the spec starts with an IP)
starter: string Reach(string publish, string listenAddress, int listenPort)
solution: string Reach(string publish, string listenAddress, int listenPort)
return "unreachable: app listens on 127.0.0.1 inside the container; bind to 0.0.0.0";
return $"unreachable: app listens on {listenPort} but {containerPort} is published";
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("happy path", "http://localhost:8080", Reach("8080:80", "0.0.0.0", 80));
Dojo.Eq("nothing published", "unreachable: no port published", Reach("", "0.0.0.0", 80));
Dojo.Eq("app bound to loopback", "unreachable: app listens on 127.0.0.1 inside the container; bind to 0.0.0.0", Reach("8080:80", "127.0.0.1", 80));
Dojo.Eq("wrong container port", "unreachable: app listens on 3000 but 80 is published", Reach("8080:80", "0.0.0.0", 3000));
hints: The container port is always the last `:` part; the host port is the one before it.
A 3-part spec means the first part is the host IP.

steps.title: Read the STATUS column
prompt: Write `string Explain(string status)` for a `docker ps -a` STATUS value:
| starts with `Up` and contains `(unhealthy)` | `running but failing its health check` |
| starts with `Restarting` | `crash loop: read docker logs` |
| `Exited (0) ...` | `finished normally: is the main process meant to keep running?` |
| `Exited (137) ...` | `killed (SIGKILL): out of memory or docker kill` |
| `Exited (N) ...` other N | `crashed with code N: read docker logs` |
solution: return status.Contains("(unhealthy)") ? "running but failing its health check" : "running";
if (status.StartsWith("Restarting")) return "crash loop: read docker logs";
"0" => "finished normally: is the main process meant to keep running?",
"137" => "killed (SIGKILL): out of memory or docker kill",
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("Up 5 minutes", "running", Explain("Up 5 minutes"));
Dojo.Eq("Up 1 hour (unhealthy)", "running but failing its health check", Explain("Up 1 hour (unhealthy)"));
Dojo.Eq("Restarting", "crash loop: read docker logs", Explain("Restarting (1) 2 seconds ago"));
Dojo.Eq("Exited (0)", "finished normally: is the main process meant to keep running?", Explain("Exited (0) 3 seconds ago"));
Dojo.Eq("Exited (137)", "killed (SIGKILL): out of memory or docker kill", Explain("Exited (137) 1 minute ago"));
Dojo.Eq("Exited (143)", "stopped gracefully (SIGTERM)", Explain("Exited (143) 10 minutes ago"));
Dojo.Eq("Exited (1)", "crashed with code 1: read docker logs", Explain("Exited (1) 4 seconds ago"));
Dojo.Eq("Created", "not started", Explain("Created"));

steps.title: Are these the same image?
steps.prompt: A teammate's compose file says `postgres`, the server runs `docker.io/library/postgres:latest`, and a script uses `library/postgres`. Write `bool SameImage(string a, string b)` that returns `true` when both references normalise to the same registry, repository and tag (rules from lesson 1: registry if the first segment has `.` or `:` or is `localhost`, default `docker.io`; tag after a `:` that follows the last `/`, default `latest`; `library/` added on `docker.io` when the repository has no `/`).
solution: bool SameImage(string a, string b) => Normalize(a) == Normalize(b);
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("postgres vs the full name", true, SameImage("postgres", "docker.io/library/postgres:latest"));
Dojo.Eq("library/postgres vs postgres:latest", true, SameImage("library/postgres", "postgres:latest"));
Dojo.Eq("different tags", false, SameImage("postgres:16", "postgres:17"));
Dojo.Eq("same repo, different registry", false, SameImage("ghcr.io/acme/api:1.0", "acme/api:1.0"));
Dojo.Eq("registry with a port", true, SameImage("localhost:5000/api", "localhost:5000/api:latest"));
Dojo.Eq("Docker Hub user repo", true, SameImage("docker.io/acme/api", "acme/api:latest"));
hints: Write a helper `string Normalize(string reference)` that returns one canonical string, then compare.
Your `ParseImage` from lesson 1 is most of the helper.
